audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer reads Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Annie/Skill/Skill; content win[] and the packet both read Lux/Lux/Skill/Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie. Five rows disagree, including levels 1-2 where the content layer is explicit that Lux wins.
audit.why: Light Binding is 1175 range and Lucent Singularity 1100 against Annie's 625 Q — levels 1-2 are Lux's for free. From level 4 the lane is Annie's because Lux has no dash and a point-and-click stun inside 625 is unanswerable. Annie's 54.37% over 1589 games matches a lane she loses early and owns after.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why and phases[6].why described generic Annie spikes on rows the full layer had marked Skill.
audit.why: The first-item row is Annie's for a concrete reason the page never gave: Lux has no mobility ability at all, so a single stun inside 625 spends her whole health bar. Final Spark is 60s at rank 1 against Tibbers at 130s, which is the real ult-trade asymmetry.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why rewritten around her lack of a dash; the 60s-versus-130s comparison added to dontsFull[2].d.
sources: enemyKit (no dash flag on any slot)

audit.whatIsWrong: Prismatic Barrier is never mentioned on the page despite being the thing that eats Annie's burst window, the Illumination auto-attack tell is absent, and "minion-block it" understates Light Binding — it passes through and binds up to TWO units, so one minion does not block it.
audit.why: Riot's Q text says the sphere binds up to two enemy units, so standing behind a single minion still leaves you rooted; two minions absorb it. Riot's passive text says her spells mark the target and her next attack detonates the mark, which makes her auto wind-up the real damage tell. Riot's W text is a straight shield on a 12s cooldown, which is the cooldown Annie should be baiting rather than the Binding.
audit.corrected: Rewrote breakdown.cooldowns, tradeBad, breakdown.trading, dosFull[1].d, phases[1].why and phases[3].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d called Light Binding a "fifteen-second" cooldown. It is 10s at every rank.
audit.why: A five-second error on the one cooldown the whole page tells you to count is a false green light — a player who steps up at ten seconds walks into a rooted combo.
audit.corrected: Corrected to a flat ten-second window, and the flat-at-every-rank fact added to breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text gives Final Spark's range as 3250; the kit file has 3340.
